title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on AI and public standards, affirming its commitment to strengthen safety, transparency, and accountability in AI systems. It outlines plans to introduce new regulations, support research, and collaborate with industry, academia, and civil society to ensure AI technologies meet high ethical and societal standards.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the EU’s new AI regulation, which sets common rules for AI use across the EU and updates existing laws to better protect people and ensure ethical AI. The government outlines how the regulation will affect businesses, consumers, and the legal framework for AI technologies.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out rules and guidelines to oversee how AI tools are used in exams and qualifications, ensuring fairness, reliability and integrity. The policy aims to protect the credibility of assessments while supporting educators and students as technology evolves.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used to train AI systems, evaluating legal, economic, and ethical implications. It offers recommendations to balance protecting creators’ rights while fostering responsible AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government responds to the House of Lords report on AI, acknowledging the urgent need to address technology’s rapid growth and avoid complacency. It outlines plans to strengthen regulation, increase research funding, and boost skills development to ensure AI is safe, fair, and benefits the UK.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the scope, objectives, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards. It also provides FAQs to help committee members understand the process and key considerations involved in the review.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence, offering its perspective on regulatory and ethical issues. The submission aims to inform policy makers on best practices and safeguards for responsible AI development.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy looks at how artificial intelligence changes the way medical products are regulated, aiming to keep them safe and effective. It applies the AI White Paper principles to set clearer guidelines for developers and regulators, making the approval process faster while protecting patients.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to position the organisation as the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑enabled defence force in the world for its size. It focuses on developing and applying advanced AI capabilities to enhance national security operations and maintain strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to unlock the benefits of AI while carefully managing its risks. It lays out strategies for innovation, safety, and regulation so that AI can improve efficiency, safety, and sustainability across the transport sector.
